rules.title: Struct pattern name must resolve
rules.statement: A struct pattern `N { .. }` requires `N` to resolve to a known struct or datatype; a type-alias `N` whose target is a Struct/ZonedStruct resolves transparently to the underlying struct (matched under the real name). Otherwise it is an error 'unknown struct'.

rules.title: Struct pattern must match scrutinee struct
rules.statement: If the scrutinee has a concrete (non-error, named) Struct type, a struct pattern's name must equal the scrutinee's struct name, else error 'struct pattern != scrutinee'.

rules.title: Struct pattern field must exist
rules.statement: Each named field in a struct pattern must be a declared field of the struct; an unknown field name is an error 'has no field'.

rules.title: Struct pattern `..` at most once and last
rules.statement: A struct pattern may contain at most one `..` rest element, and no named field may follow `..`; violations are errors.

rules.title: Struct pattern must cover all fields unless `..`
rules.statement: A non-union struct pattern without `..` must name every field of the struct; an uncovered field is an error (suggesting `..`).

rules.title: `ref [mut] f` field shorthand binds a reference to the field
rules.statement: In a struct pattern, a field marked `ref` (optionally `ref mut`) with no explicit sub-pattern binds `f` to `&[mut] T` where `T` is the field type, equivalent to a `ref [mut] f` ref-binding sub-pattern.

rules.title: Shorthand field binds the field name
rules.statement: A plain shorthand field `{ f }` (no sub-pattern) binds a new variable named `f` to the field value; `_` is non-binding.

rules.title: Literal field sub-pattern lowers to a binding plus equality guard
rules.statement: A refutable literal field sub-pattern `S { f: <int|neg-int|bool|char> }` (in refutable context) binds the field to a fresh synthetic name and gates the arm with `synth == <literal>`.

rules.title: Limited set of refutable field sub-patterns
rules.statement: Refutable field sub-patterns are accepted only for kinds {Wild, RefBind, RefPat, At, Variant, VariantData, Tuple, Or, Range, Int, Bool, Struct}; other kinds (e.g. slice, writ) are an error 'not yet supported'.
rules.uncertainty: List reflects current implementation coverage; the unsupported set is an implementation limitation rather than a settled language rule.

rules.title: Union pattern names exactly one field inside unsafe
rules.statement: A pattern on a `union` must specify exactly one field (no `..`), and the match must occur inside an `unsafe` block (it reads the named field's memory). Violations are errors.

rules.title: Slice pattern requires array/slice scrutinee
rules.statement: A slice pattern `[..]` requires the scrutinee to be of array or slice type; the element sub-patterns are typed by the element type. A non-array/slice scrutinee is an error.

rules.title: Slice pattern `..` at most once
rules.statement: A slice pattern may contain at most one `..` rest; elements before `..` form the prefix, elements after form the suffix. A second `..` is an error.

rules.title: Named `..` binds the rest sub-slice
rules.statement: A rest element written `name @ ..` binds `name` to the rest sub-slice; a bare `..` is anonymous.

rules.title: Fixed-array slice pattern length constraints
rules.statement: For a fixed-size array scrutinee: a slice pattern without `..` must have exactly `N` elements; with `..`, prefix+suffix count must not exceed `N`. Violations are errors.

rules.title: Writ scalar patterns only in match arms
rules.statement: Writ scalar patterns (`@null`, `@true`, `@false`, `@<int>`, `@"str"`, `@{...}`, `@[...]`, and typed array/map forms) are permitted only in `match` arms, not in if-let / while-let / let-bindings / nested pattern positions; elsewhere is an error. In a match arm they lower to a wildcard plus a synthesized guard.
rules.divergence: Logos extension (Writ value patterns); no Rust equivalent.

rules.title: Bare ident resolving to a use-imported nullary variant is a variant pattern
rules.statement: A bare identifier pattern that matches a `use Type.{V, ..}` variant alias and names a nullary (no-payload) variant is a variant pattern, not a fresh binding; the scrutinee enum must match, else error.

rules.title: Bare ident resolving to a module const is a value pattern
rules.statement: A bare identifier that names a module-level const is a value (refutable) pattern, not a binding: its initializer is ctfe-evaluated and matched. Bool/int/char consts emit a literal pattern. A non-ctfe-evaluable const initializer is an error.

rules.title: str-typed const pattern lowers to a str_eq guard
rules.statement: A const pattern of `str` (Slice<u8>) type against a str scrutinee binds a synthetic name and gates the arm with `str_eq(synth, CONST)`; requires the stdlib `str_eq` to be in scope, else error.

rules.title: [u8; N] const pattern lowers to an element-wise equality guard
rules.statement: A const pattern of `[u8; N]` type against a `[u8; N]` scrutinee (matching array length) binds a synthetic name and gates the arm with the AND-chain `synth[i] == CONST[i]` for all i in 0..N.

rules.title: Other non-scalar const patterns rejected
rules.statement: A const pattern whose value is neither int/bool/char nor the supported str/[u8;N] guard cases is an error ('non-scalar type').
rules.uncertainty: Reflects current support boundary, not a permanent language restriction.

rules.title: Bare ident is a binding; `mut` recorded for mutable binding
rules.statement: A bare identifier not resolving to a variant or const is a fresh binding (`_` is non-binding/wildcard). A `mut x` binding is recorded so the binding is introduced as mutable.
